Portfolio Project Instructions (Dipankar Kumar — "Learn what the problem needs, then build it."):
1. Documentation Hierarchy: Follow the source-of-truth priority: (1) Explicit instruction from Dipankar, (2) docs/PRD.md, (3) docs/DESIGN.md, (4) docs/CONTENT.md, (5) docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, (6) docs/TECH_STACK.md, (7) docs/DEVELOPMENT_RULES.md, (8) Existing implementation. Stop and ask before making major architectural changes, introducing frameworks/backends/databases, or adding unapproved dependencies.
2. Content Integrity & Attribution: Never fabricate or exaggerate experience, job titles, metrics, technologies, or achievements. docs/CONTENT.md is the sole source of truth. Accurately distinguish collaborative from individual work. Position Dipankar as an early-career software engineer learning what the problem needs and building it, never as a senior engineer or specialized ML expert. Never expose private personal data.
3. Architecture & Design: Keep implementation data-driven and clean. Portfolio data lives in typed TypeScript modules in src/data/ separated from UI components. Adhere strictly to the Picto-inspired design direction (clean typography, generous whitespace, structured grid, restrained interaction; no 3D/WebGL/flashy gimmicks).
4. Verification & Scope: Keep changes focused with zero unrequested scope creep. Always verify with `npm run build` and check responsive layouts across mobile, tablet, and desktop before concluding any task. Never claim untested functionality works.

Portfolio Core Governance & RECALL Documentation Requirements (Updated for V2.6):

1. Documentation Hierarchy & Source of Truth:
   - Priority: (1) Explicit instruction from Dipankar, (2) docs/PRD.md, (3) docs/DESIGN.md, (4) docs/CONTENT.md, (5) docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, (6) docs/TECH_STACK.md, (7) docs/DEVELOPMENT_RULES.md, (8) Existing implementation.
   - Stop and ask before making major architectural changes, introducing frameworks/backends/databases, or adding unapproved dependencies.

2. Content Integrity & Attribution:
   - Never fabricate or exaggerate experience, job titles, metrics, technologies, or achievements. docs/CONTENT.md and src/data/*.ts are canonical.
   - Accurately distinguish collaborative from individual work. Position Dipankar as an early-career software engineer ("I learn what the problem needs and build it."). Never expose private data or credentials.

3. Architecture & Design Discipline (V2.6 Accepted State):
   - Keep implementation data-driven in typed TypeScript modules (`src/data/`) separated from UI components (`src/components/`, `src/sections/`).
   - Preserve the accepted V2.6 Engineering Notebook Paper & Graphite design: `paper-background.webp` (`#F5F2EB`) + `paper-card.webp` (`#FAF8F3`), porous double-pass `#pencil-stroke-primary`/`#pencil-stroke-fine` SVG filters, delicate corner grazes, hatched exterior graphite smudges, `DP` branding, and the hand-drawn pencil `ScrollToTop` control. Do NOT revert to v1.8 3D/frosted glass or add Tailwind/Three.js.

4. Verification, Scope & Session Startup:
   - Before starting work, retrieve `PORTFOLIO_V2.6_MASTER_INDEX` and relevant V2.6 RECALL memories.
   - Always verify with `npm run build` and check responsive viewports (`1920`, `1440`, `1280`, `1024`, `768`, `390`, `360px`) before concluding. Record milestones, root causes, and honest verification status in RECALL.
